# Public benchmark and checkpoint provenance

Downloads/audit: 2026-09-18. All image/mask files remain on the public-data pod. `release-manifest.json` pins the exact downloaded source bytes; cohort audits pin metadata, normalized masks and all three subject splits. These hashes do not establish clinical consent beyond the publishers' public release terms.

BrEaST / Breast-Lesions-USG Version 1 (TCIA, updated 2024-01-08): Pawłowska, A., Ćwierz-Pieńkowska, A., Domalik, A., Jaguś, D., Kasprzak, P., Matkowski, R., Fura, Ł., Nowicki, A., and Żołek, N. (2024), *A Curated Benchmark Dataset for Ultrasound Based Breast Lesion Analysis*, DOI [10.7937/9WKK-Q141](https://doi.org/10.7937/9WKK-Q141). Related descriptor: *Scientific Data* 11, 148, DOI [10.1038/s41597-024-02984-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-024-02984-z). [TCIA collection](https://www.cancerimagingarchive.net/collection/breast-lesions-usg/) declares CC BY 4.0. The published scan/patient relationship and the XLSX CaseID/Image_filename mapping support 256 subjects. The binary target unions the primary tumor and other suspicious lesions. Four publisher-declared normal cases receive explicit empty annotations; absent masks without that declaration would remain invalid.

BUS-BRA v1.0: Gómez-Flores, W., Gregorio-Calas, M. J., and Pereira, W. C. A. (2024), *BUS-BRA: A Breast Ultrasound Dataset for Assessing Computer-aided Diagnosis Systems*, *Medical Physics* 51, 3110–3123, DOI [10.1002/mp.16812](https://doi.org/10.1002/mp.16812). Dataset DOI [10.5281/zenodo.8231412](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8231412), [official metadata API](https://zenodo.org/api/records/8231412). The record explicitly declares CC BY 4.0; the ZIP additionally contains a permissive attribution licence preserved verbatim in `BUS-BRA-LICENSE.txt`. Both require attribution; neither is replaced with the source-code repository's separate GPL licence. The released Case column exactly spans 1..1064, agrees with all filename prefixes, and groups both official 5-fold/10-fold test partitions. This is the audited mapping used for patient grouping. No inference from image count alone is made.

Mask normalization is a format conversion on these public releases, preserving native pixel geometry: identical RGB silhouettes from BrEaST RGBA masks become L-mode {0,255}; BUS-BRA boolean masks become the same vocabulary. Every converted mask retains its source and output SHA256 in the audit. BrEaST's per-image annotations are retained as separate source rows; their union is performed by the trusted subject loader.

Checkpoint: [torchvision ResNet18 IMAGENET1K_V1](https://docs.pytorch.org/vision/0.19/models/generated/torchvision.models.resnet18.html), source URL `https://download.pytorch.org/models/resnet18-f37072fd.pth`, SHA256 `f37072fd47e89c5e827621c5baffa7500819f7896bbacec160b1a16c560e07ec`. The torch/torchvision runtime used on the pod is 2.4.1/0.19.1. `torchvision-LICENSE.txt` records the BSD software licence. Upstream [model terms](https://docs.pytorch.org/vision/0.19/models.html#general-information-on-pre-trained-weights) state that pretrained weights may carry training-dataset-specific conditions; software BSD is not asserted as a universal weight licence. The protocol uses the upstream checkpoint for public academic benchmarking, records those terms, and neither packages nor redistributes the pretrained tensors. The pinned spatial 128-grid transform differs deliberately from the stock 224-grid classification crop; every federation/twin uses the contract transform.
